source_title: Jemimah Rodrigues declared fit after three months of hamstring rehabilitation - Sportstar
source_excerpt:
Jemimah Rodrigues’ injury forced her to miss the Women’s Asia Cup and the Asian Games before also ruling her out of India’s recent white-ball series against Zimbabwe. | Photo Credit: GETTY IMAGES
India batter Jemimah Rodrigues has been declared fit after three months of rehabilitation following a high-grade tear in her right hamstring, sustained while playing for Southern Brave in The Hundred in England on August 3.
Jemimah shared the update on social media on Friday, expressing her eagerness to return to action after completing her recovery.
“Life Update: HAMSTRING HAS BEEN DECLARED FIT!!!!!!!! After 3 months of rehab. Now I can’t wait to get going,” she wrote.
A post shared by Jemimah Jessica Rodrigues (@jemimahrodrigues)
The injury brought an abrupt end to Jemimah’s campaign in The Hundred, where she had scored 143 runs in six innings and put on two Player-of-the-Match performances.
Jemimah was injured while playing against Welsh Fire, with the setback subsequently confirmed by the BCCI as a high-grade tear. The injury forced her to miss the Women’s Asia Cup and the Asian Games before also ruling her out of India’s recent white-ball series against Zimbabwe.
With her recovery now complete, Jemimah could be in contention for India’s multi-format tour of South Africa in December.
